$comment: Fluid hosted-docs evaluation set, graded by eval/check-hosted-docs.mjs in two stages. Stage 1 (retrieval) asks the hosted /mcp search_fluid tool the prompt text and passes when the page that documents the answer is among the returned pages; for API prompts that page is resolved mechanically from llms-full.txt by matching the generated contract line <method> <path>, and for workflow prompts it is declared as target_page (a string or an array when a workflow legitimately spans a guide plus the reference it points at). Stage 2 (contract) fetches that page's full markdown and checks the contract there, not in the search snippet: method, path, auth, required_query_params (matched as the inlined spec's `name: <param>` form), and required_body_fields (matched as the schema-property `<field>:` form) for API prompts; required_terms and forbidden_terms for workflow prompts. auth is derived from the page's inlined security requirement (`- bearer_auth: []`), never from prose, because every page opens with a banner naming the Bearer header. Splitting the stages keeps a discoverability failure distinguishable from a correctness failure, and page-scoping makes forbidden_terms meaningful: a name absent from the page that owns the workflow is a real assertion, where its absence from a ten-page search dump was not. All API expectations are verified against the synced specs; SDK and theme workflow expectations are verified against the durable Phase 9.6 decisions. Retrieved content and every fetched target page are also scanned for legacy endpoint leakage. Notes cite operationIds, schema names, and literal spec declarations, never spec line numbers: the specs re-sync hourly, so line references rot and a stale one lands a reader on the wrong operation.

prompts.prompt: I'm building an unauthenticated storefront browse page. What API call lists the categories that are live on a company's public storefront? I just need the public catalog for the current shop, no login.
prompts.notes: Public Categories catalog. storefrontCategoriesIndex, security: []. Company resolved from subdomain, so no auth.

prompts.prompt: I have a collection's URL slug ("wellness-essentials") and need to render that single collection on a public, no-login storefront page. What's the request to fetch it by slug?
prompts.notes: Public Collection by slug. storefrontCollectionShow, security: []. Resolves by slug path param.

prompts.prompt: As a company admin with an API bearer token, how do I create a brand-new category titled "Summer Sale"?
prompts.notes: Create a Category. companyCategoriesCreate, bearer_auth. Body wrapped in `category`; required field is `title` (CategoryCreateRequest).

prompts.prompt: Using our company admin token, I need to rename an existing collection (id 5102) to "Holiday Picks". What's the exact request?
prompts.notes: Update a Collection. companyCollectionsUpdate uses PATCH, bearer_auth. Body wrapped in `collection`; rename sets `title` (CollectionWrite).

prompts.prompt: On the public (no-auth) storefront, fetch the first 50 top-level categories that are available in the United Kingdom, returned in French, sorted alphabetically by title (A to Z). What's the full request with query parameters?
prompts.notes: Public Categories catalog with filters. filter[country]=GB, filter[language]=fr, filter[parent_id]=root for top-level, sort=title, page[limit]=50. All names verified verbatim.

prompts.prompt: How do I permanently delete the category with id 4821 as a company admin (I have a bearer token)?
prompts.notes: Destroy a Category. companyCategoriesDestroy, DELETE, bearer_auth, returns 204.

prompts.prompt: I want the category with id 4821 to automatically go live at 2026-08-01T08:00:00Z. As a company admin, what single call schedules it to publish at that time?
prompts.notes: Scheduling is done via update (there is no separate publish endpoint). companyCategoriesUpdate PATCH, bearer. Set status=scheduled + publish_at (CategoryWrite). Body wrapped in `category`.

prompts.prompt: We're only selling a collection (id 5102) in Great Britain and the United States. As a company admin, how do I restrict that collection's country availability to just GB and US?
prompts.notes: Country availability is a write field, not a query param, on the company surface. Spec CollectionWrite: country_isos array restricts availability. Set via companyCollectionsUpdate PATCH. Body wrapped in `collection`.

prompts.prompt: On the public storefront, how do I fetch only the child categories nested directly under the parent category whose id is 4821?
prompts.notes: Hierarchy / children-of filter. filter[parent_id] takes a category id (or 'root' for top-level). Only exists on the public categories index, not the company index. Value would be 4821.

prompts.prompt: As a company admin, how do I pull the aggregate share statistics for the category with id 4821?
prompts.notes: Share statistics for a Category. companyCategoriesShares, GET, bearer_auth, read-only aggregate.

prompts.prompt: I'm building an email login screen. When a user types their email address, what API call sends them a one-time login passcode by email? No user is signed in yet.
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_send_mfa. `email` is a required query param; `fluid_shop` is optional; security: [] (no auth). Auth paths are unversioned /api/... (not v202604).

prompts.prompt: After we emailed the passcode, the user entered their code. I have the MFA uuid returned from the send step. What request confirms the code and returns the JWTs for the user's companies?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_confirm_mfa. Request body requires `uuid` plus `multi_factor_authentication.verification_code`; security: [] (no auth). Grader flattens nested body keys, so the leaf `verification_code` matches.

prompts.prompt: On our public sign-in page I want to show a company's name and logo before anyone logs in. Given the shop name "acme-wellness", what unauthenticated call returns that company's basic public details?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_company_details. `fluid_shop` is a path param; security: [] (public). Returns CompanyPublicDetails.

prompts.prompt: My server-side integration already holds a user-company token and needs a regular user JWT to call authenticated endpoints (this is not a customer session). What request exchanges that user-company token for a JWT?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_token_exchange. Body requires `user_company_token`; security: [] because the token travels in the body, not the Authorization header. Disambiguated from customer_token_exchange (customer JWT) and jwt_exchange (reverse direction).

prompts.prompt: Our session JWT is about to expire. What single call refreshes an existing JWT to extend its validity?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_jwt_refresh. Body requires `jwt`; security: [] (the JWT to refresh is supplied in the body).

prompts.prompt: I want to render the available social login buttons (Google, Apple, Facebook) for the shop "acme-wellness" on the login page. What call lists the social auth providers and their OAuth URLs for that shop?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_social_auth_providers. `fluid_shop` is a required query param; security: [] (public).

prompts.prompt: A signed-in user belongs to several companies and picked company 512 to switch into. Using their bearer token, what call switches the authenticated user to that company and returns a fresh JWT?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_switch_company. `company_id` is a path param; security: bearer_auth. Distinct from GET /api/authentication/company/{fluid_shop} (public branding).

prompts.prompt: As a Fluid root admin with a bearer token, how do I start impersonating the company with id 42?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/auth-v0.yaml, operationId auth_v0_impersonate_company. Body requires `company_id`; security: bearer_auth (root admins only). Returns 201 with the impersonation JWT.

prompts.prompt: I'm building the very first step of checkout — no customer is logged in yet. For shop "acme-wellness", what request creates a brand-new cart for a US-based shopper?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_create_cart. Required body fields: fluid_shop, country_code. security: [] — cart creation is unauthenticated.

prompts.prompt: A shopper picked a size and color variant on the product page and I already have their cart token. What request adds that variant and quantity to the existing cart?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_add_cart_items. Top-level required body field is `items`, an array of {variant_id, quantity} entries. AUTH CORRECTED from bearer to none: the operation declares an explicit `security: []`, so it is unauthenticated. These cart endpoints are credentialed by the opaque cart token in the path — the generated page states "cart-token authentication carried in the path, with no bearer token or API key". The old note claimed `security: bearer_auth`, which the synced spec contradicts. Cite the operationId rather than spec line numbers: the spec is re-synced hourly, so line references rot.

prompts.prompt: A shopper typed the promo code SAVE10 into the cart's discount field. Using the cart token, what request applies that code to the cart?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_apply_cart_discount. Required body field: discount_code. AUTH CORRECTED from bearer to none: the operation declares an explicit `security: []`, so it is unauthenticated; the cart token in the path is the credential. The old note claimed `security: bearer_auth`, which the synced spec contradicts. Not idempotent — reapplying the same code errors.

prompts.prompt: Before showing the email-confirmation step at checkout, I want to silently check whether the email a shopper just typed belongs to an existing customer — without creating a new account if it doesn't. What request performs that returning-buyer probe on the cart?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_send_cart_magic_link. Required body fields: email, fluid_shop. The probe behavior is the optional `lookup_only: true` flag — a 404 means no existing customer, telling the frontend to treat the email as a guest and skip the confirmation step. AUTH CORRECTED from bearer to none: operationId checkout_v2026_04_send_cart_magic_link declares an explicit `security: []`, so it is unauthenticated; the cart token in the path is the credential. The old note claimed `security: bearer_auth`, which the synced spec contradicts.

prompts.prompt: A shopper on cart cart_9f2 wants to convert one of the cart's variants into a recurring subscription, billing to their saved address going forward. What request creates that subscription?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_create_subscription (spec, distinct from the GET list at). Body wrapped in `subscription`; required nested fields: subscription_plan_id, customer_id, variant_id, address_id, cart_token, timezone, next_bill_date. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: A customer on an active subscription (token sb_5567) wants to bump their recurring item quantity from 1 to 2. Using the subscription token, what request updates just the quantity?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_update_subscription. Body must be wrapped in a `subscription` object (required, minProperties 1); `quantity` is one of its writable properties. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: A customer just finished checkout and landed on the order-confirmation page carrying an order token in the URL. What unauthenticated request fetches that order to render the confirmation?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_get_order. security: [] — explicitly documented as a public endpoint, no authentication required.

prompts.prompt: A prospect clicked an enrollment link carrying a token and needs to see the enrollment form before filling it out. What public request retrieves that enrollment by token?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/checkout-v2026-04.yaml, operationId checkout_v2026_04_get_enrollment. security: [] — public endpoint per spec description.

prompts.prompt: As a platform admin with a Fluid payment API key (fp_live_...), how do I list all the payment gateways configured for my merchant?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId listGateways. Global security is bearer_auth; the API key travels as a bearer token, so auth=bearer. Admin gateway surface is /api/payment/v2026-04 (singular 'payment'), distinct from the cart /api/payments flow.

prompts.prompt: Using my payment API key, I need to register a new Stripe credit-card gateway for the US. What request creates a payment gateway?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId createGateway. Body is wrapped in a required `gateway` object; GatewayCreateRequest requires name + integration_type. Grader flattens nested keys, so the `gateway` wrapper is fine. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: I need to change the country codes and credentials on an existing payment gateway (slug stripe-usd) using my payment API key. What's the request to update it?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId updateGateway, PATCH (not PUT). Body wrapped in a `gateway` object holding GatewayUpdateRequest (all fields optional), so no field is individually required. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: How do I permanently remove a payment gateway (slug stripe-usd) from my merchant using the payment admin API key?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId destroyGateway, DELETE, returns 204. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: As a merchant with my payment API key, I want to immediately charge $49.99 USD against a saved payment method through my Stripe gateway (slug stripe-usd) — a one-step sale, not an authorization I capture later. What request runs the purchase?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId purchaseGateway. Body wrapped in a required `transaction` object; TransactionRequest requires amount_cents + currency_code. Purchase = immediate sale, distinct from authorize. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: Through my Stripe gateway (slug stripe-usd), I want to authorize (hold) $49.99 USD now and capture it later once the item ships. Using my payment API key, what request creates the authorization?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId authorizeGateway. Body wrapped in a required `transaction` object; TransactionRequest requires amount_cents + currency_code. Authorize = hold-for-later-capture, distinct from purchase (immediate sale). security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: I previously authorized a payment and now want to capture the funds. Given the authorization's transaction id, what request captures it using my payment API key?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId captureTransaction. Path is the transaction id (the authorization), not a gateway. Body is optional — omit `transaction.amount_cents` for a full capture, supply it for a partial — so no field is required. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: A customer needs a refund on a completed charge. Given that charge's transaction id, what request issues a refund/credit against it using my payment API key?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId creditTransaction. Refund is the `credit` action on the original transaction. Body optional — omit `transaction.amount_cents` for a full refund, supply it for a partial — so no field is required. Distinct from void (which cancels an uncaptured authorization). security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: Using my payment API key, how do I read my merchant's payment configuration — the VGS, Kount, 3DS acquirer, and payout settings — for merchant id 1024?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payment-v2026-04.yaml, operationId showMerchantConfiguration. Secret fields are returned obfuscated; API-key auth is scoped to the authenticated merchant. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: In checkout I have a cart token and a VGS-tokenized credit card. What request sets the payment method on that cart? No JWT or API key is involved — just the cart.
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_set_payment_method, PUT (idempotent). Only `type` is required; other fields vary by payment type. security: [] — the cart token in the path is the credential, no bearer. Cart flow lives under /api/payments (plural), distinct from the /api/payment admin surface.

prompts.prompt: Before collecting card details in checkout, I need the VGS Collect vault credentials to tokenize the card client-side. Given the cart token, what request provisions the VGS vault?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_tokenize. No request body — it resolves the CreditCard payment account and returns VGS vault credentials. security: [] — cart-token in path, no bearer.

prompts.prompt: The card on my cart needs a 3D Secure check. Using the cart token, what request kicks off 3DS device fingerprinting and returns the 3DS method content?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_verify. Request body is optional (an explicit vgs_card_id fallback, otherwise resolved from the cart's payment method), so no field is required. security: [] — cart-token in path, no bearer.

prompts.prompt: A shopper chose PayPal in checkout. Using the cart token, what request creates the PayPal order for a standard (not pay-later) PayPal funding source?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_paypal_create_order. Required body fields: funding_source + is_pay_later. security: [] — cart-token in path, no bearer.

prompts.prompt: I'm initializing the Braintree JS SDK on the checkout page and need a Braintree client token. Given the cart token and the Braintree payment account UUID, what request returns the client token?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_braintree_client_token, GET. payment_account_id is a required query param. security: [] — cart-token in path, no bearer.

prompts.prompt: A shopper selected Klarna in checkout. Using the cart token, what request creates the Klarna payment session and returns its client token?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_klarna_create_session, POST. Request body is optional (an optional `intent` string), so no field is required. Distinct from the PATCH update on the same path (payments_v2026_04_klarna_update_session, which requires session_id). security: [] — cart-token in path, no bearer.

prompts.prompt: During Apple Pay checkout the onvalidatemerchant event fired with an Apple session URL. Using the cart token, what request validates the Apple Pay merchant session?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/payments-v2026-04.yaml, operationId payments_v2026_04_apple_pay_validate. Required body fields: company_id, country_id, apple_session_url. Requires a Referer matching a verified domain. security: [] — cart-token in path, no bearer.

prompts.prompt: After an order is already placed, I need to atomically add a line item and a fee adjustment to it in one transaction using my company bearer token. Given the order id, what request commits the order edit?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/commerce-v2026-04.yaml, operationId commerce_v2026_04_create_order_edit. Required body field: operations (array, applied atomically) — OrderEditRequest requires operations; requestBody required. security: bearer_auth. Commits and fires the order_edited webhook, distinct from the /preview dry-run.

prompts.prompt: I'm building a droplet that adds a free gift to an existing order: insert the gift variant at $29.99 and an offsetting -$29.99 credit adjustment so the total is unchanged, committed together. Using the droplet's bearer token and the order id, what single request applies this?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/commerce-v2026-04.yaml, operationId commerce_v2026_04_create_order_edit — the free-gift flow is the documented use case (insert_item + add_adjustment in one operations array). Required body field: operations. Droplet installation tokens are bearer credentials and are exempt from granular override permission checks. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: Before I commit an order edit, I want a dry-run that returns the recalculated order totals without persisting anything — no audit records, no webhooks. Using my company bearer token and the order id, what request previews the edit?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/commerce-v2026-04.yaml, operationId commerce_v2026_04_preview_order_edit. Same OrderEditRequest body (required operations) as the commit endpoint, but runs inside an always-rolled-back savepoint and returns dry_run: true. security: bearer_auth. Distinct path (/edits/preview) from the committing /edits endpoint.

prompts.prompt: As a company admin with a bearer token, I want Fluid to POST to my endpoint every time an order is created. What request registers that webhook subscription?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_create_webhook. Body wrapped in `webhook`; required fields url, resource, event. security: bearer_auth. Unversioned /api/... path (webhooks-v0 is not versioned).

prompts.prompt: Using our company bearer token, how do I list all the webhook subscriptions currently registered for our company?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_index_webhooks. security: bearer_auth. Unversioned /api/... path.

prompts.prompt: I have a webhook's numeric id (8123) and want to fetch that single subscription as a company admin. What's the request?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_show_webhook. `id` is a path param; security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: I want to temporarily disable a webhook (id 8123) without deleting it, using our company token. What request turns it off?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_update_webhook. Update uses PUT (not PATCH). Body wrapped in `webhook`; set active:false to deactivate — the update body accepts url, active, auth_token, http_method (not resource/event). security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: How do I permanently remove the webhook subscription with id 8123 as a company admin?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_destroy_webhook. security: bearer_auth. Returns 200 echoing {webhook:{id}}.

prompts.prompt: I want to confirm the most recent order webhook Fluid delivered to us. As a company admin, what call returns the latest delivered event for the order resource?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_webhook_resource_events. `resource_name` is a path param (e.g. order); returns the most recent delivered event envelope for that resource. 404 for an unregistered resource. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: Our droplet needs Fluid to call us synchronously for tax calculation. Using our company bearer token, what request registers a callback registration pointing at our URL?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_create_callback_registration. Body wrapped in `callback_registration`; required fields definition_name, url. Returns 409 if a registration for that definition already exists for the owner. security: bearer_auth.

prompts.prompt: Before building a handler, I want the published JSON payload schema for the order_created event. As a company admin, what call returns that event's schema?
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/webhooks-v0.yaml, operationId webhooks_v0_get_api_webhooks_schemas_by_event_identifier. `event_identifier` is a path param (e.g. order_created); returns the latest schema for that event. security: bearer_auth. Unversioned /api/webhooks/... path.

prompts.prompt: I already have a product (id 60311) in our store's default language. As a company admin with a bearer token, how do I translate that existing product into French — set its French title and description?
prompts.notes: Translate an existing product. Writing a translation is always a company PATCH on the existing row with the target locale in `lang` (LangWrite, spec) — NOT a create. Spec companyProductsUpdate, bearer_auth. `lang=fr` selects the write locale; body wrapped in `product` carries the translated title/description. Guide: api/guides/translate-resources.mdx.

prompts.prompt: Our company API token is ready. I want to add a Spanish name and description to an existing product without touching its slug, price, or status. What's the exact request?
prompts.notes: Add a Spanish translation to a product. Same write path as any translation: PATCH the existing product with `lang=es` (LangWrite, spec); a non-default-locale PATCH writes only the translated text fields, so slug/price/status are untouched. Spec companyProductsUpdate, bearer_auth. Guide: api/guides/translate-resources.mdx.

prompts.prompt: I need to translate one of our media items into French — give it a French title and description. I have a company admin bearer token. What's the request? Note: I want to actually store the French translation, not just view the catalog in French.
prompts.notes: Translate a media item — the classic mis-route. Writing a media translation is the company update PATCH with the target locale in `lang` (LangWrite, spec region; companyMediumUpdate). The public GET /api/v202604/media only RENDERS (`lang`) and FILTERS (`filter[language]`) locales — it never writes one. Body wrapped in `medium`; bearer_auth. Guide: api/guides/translate-resources.mdx.

prompts.prompt: As a company admin (bearer token in hand), how do I add a Spanish translation of a category's name and description to an existing category?
prompts.notes: Translate a category. Same model as every resource: PATCH the existing company row with `lang=es` (LangWrite); companyCategoriesUpdate, bearer_auth. Body wrapped in `category`; a non-default-locale PATCH writes only the translated text. Guide: api/guides/translate-resources.mdx.

prompts.prompt: I'm tracing the SDK-internal browser request that the FairShare SDK uses to create a US cart for canyon-co.fluid.app. What public-v2025-06 API call does it make, and which fields are required? This is not a new direct REST integration; those should use Checkout v2026-04.
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/public-v2025-06.yaml, operationId public_v2025_06_cart-create. The operation declares security: [], requestBody required: true, and CartCreateRequestBodyApplicationJsonSchema requires country_code and fluid_shop. This is the FairShare SDK's SDK-internal cart surface; new direct REST integrations use checkout-v2026-04.

prompts.prompt: I'm debugging the SDK-internal FairShare call that turns an existing cart token into an order. Which public-v2025-06 method and path complete the cart, and does it require a Bearer token? A new direct REST checkout would use Checkout v2026-04 instead.
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/public-v2025-06.yaml, operationId public_v2025_06_cart-checkout. The cart_token path parameter is required, the operation declares security: [], and it declares no request body. This completes the FairShare SDK's SDK-internal cart lifecycle; new direct REST integrations use checkout-v2026-04.

prompts.prompt: I'm tracing the SDK-internal FairShare utility that loads active checkout and order-confirmation drop zones for canyon-co.fluid.app. What API call does it make, which query field is required, and is authentication needed? Direct REST integrations should use the Checkout v2026-04 drop-zones operation.
prompts.notes: Verified against api-reference/public-v2025-06.yaml, operationId public_v2025_06_index_public_drop_zones. The operation declares security: [] and the fluid_shop query parameter as required: true. Its generated description identifies this as SDK-internal and directs REST integrations to checkout-v2026-04.

prompts.prompt: I'm rendering a product bundle selector in a storefront theme. From the published product object, which collection contains the bundle groups, and which exact group fields tell me the group type, the selection rules, and the selectable items?
prompts.notes: CURRENT-2711 bundle discovery prompt, corrected because the original expectations could never pass. It required the legacy product_bundle_groups shape that themes/product-bundles explicitly disavows ("Use product.bundle_groups[], not the legacy product.product_bundle_groups[] shape"), so the required term is now the dotted product.bundle_groups — the legacy name does not contain that substring, so it cannot satisfy the check. It also required pricing_type and country_pricing, which appear in no published page and not in storefront-v2026-04.yaml; guide-truth Phase 9.6c.1 records exhaustive bundle pricing and country configuration as accepted reference territory, so those requirements contradicted a durable decision. Remaining group fields verified in storefront-v2026-04.yaml ProductBundleGroup: group_type, min_selections, max_selections, selection_type, bundle_group_items, and item bundled_variant_id. group_type is spec-only — it reaches readers through the generated Product show reference, not the prose page or llms-full.txt. product_bundles_attributes was dropped as a forbidden term: it is a current, correctly documented company-write field (static-bundle component links), so scanning retrieved content for it fails on correct docs. product_bundle_groups is deliberately NOT forbidden for the same reason — the page names it in a corrective warning, and the subscriptions spec exposes subscription.variant.product.product_bundle_groups[]. Two target pages because this workflow legitimately spans two synced contracts (Phase 9.6c.1): the theme guide supplies the render shape and the generated storefront Product show reference supplies the spec-only group_type. product_bundles_attributes is restored as a forbidden term now that the scan is page-scoped — it is verified absent from both target pages, so its absence is a real assertion again.
